children: , the Chinese commerce and cloud AI company, outlined its next AI push as its U.S. shares fell about 4.5% to $111.105 Wednesday morning. The plan pairs a model with 5 trillion to 10 trillion parameters with a new chip built to handle larger AI workloads.

The chip, called Zhenwu V900, delivers three times the performance of its predecessor, according to Alibaba's announcement reported by AP. Alibaba says it can connect up to 500,000 chips in a cluster. The company is also aiming for more than 20 gigawatts of global data center capacity by 2032. Big numbers. But building the capacity and filling it with paying customers are two different jobs.

The chart shows a GF Value of $121.30, putting the $111.105 share price about 8.4% below that estimate. The discount is interesting; the return on all this AI spending matters more. Investors need to see whether Alibaba's models and chips can drive enough profitable cloud demand to support its expansion.

title: Alibaba Drops 4.5% as Ten-Trillion Parameters Raise the Power Bill
